questions.question: Which ACL-matrix slice should run on every standard run (full 151-route × 6-role sweep stays nightly)?

options.label: Critical routes × all roles
options.description: A curated allowlist of the most sensitive routes (admin, users, id_documents, cashDeposits/depositRequests, credit-lines, operations) checked across all 6 roles. ~20s. Best at catching privilege-escalation regressions (a sensitive route opening up to a low-priv role). Recommended.

options.label: All routes × anonymous only
options.description: Every auth route must reject the unauthenticated user (302/403), checked every run. ~70s. Proves nothing is publicly reachable, but only the unauthenticated dimension and adds notable time.

options.label: Critical routes, anon + beneficiary
options.description: Curated sensitive routes checked against just the two lowest-privilege actors (anonymous + beneficiary). ~10s, fastest. Narrower role coverage than option 1.

Done. Here's what I changed and verified.

## What I did

I measured the suite first (full run with JUnit timing in an isolated test slot), and the data was decisive — **~17 min sequential, with 4 classes accounting for 60% of it**. You picked the ≥50s cut, so those 4 are now the nightly group.

**Tagged `@group nightly`** (matching the repo's existing docblock convention):
| Class | Time |
|---|---|
| `AclMatrixTest` | 423s (full route×role sweep) |
| `PDFTest` | 82s |
| `SmokeTest` | 63s |
| `OperationsControllerTest` | 54s |

**Wired it up:**
- `phpunit.xml` — added `<group>nightly</group>` to the `<exclude>` block, so the default `php artisan test` / `bin/test.sh` skips them.
- `bin/test-nightly.sh` (new) — runs `--group=nightly`, which overrides the config exclude. Delegates to `test.sh` so it reuses the Vite-build refresh + container autodetection.
- `CLAUDE.md` — documented the split and how to re-rank slow tests.

## Verified (via `php artisan test`, not just raw phpunit)
- **Default run** → 2186 tests (nightly excluded). `--filter=PDFTest` reports *"No tests found"* ✓
- **`--group=nightly`** → exactly the 4 classes (119 tests); ran PDFTest's 36 → all pass ✓
- `2186 + 119 = 2305`, and the full suite was green in the measurement run.

## Two things worth knowing
1. **There was a real bug in my first attempt**: PHPUnit treats the *entire line* after `@group` as the group name, so `@group nightly Slow (...)` registered a group literally named `"nightly Slow (...)"` and matched nothing. I moved the prose to a separate line — `@group nightly` now stands alone. (Worth remembering if anyone tags more.)
2. **Deprecation**: PHPUnit 11.5 honors `@group` docblocks but warns they go away in PHPUnit 12 (this already affects the repo's existing `QaBugs20260520Test`). I kept docblocks to match convention; migrating all `@group` usage to `#[Group(...)]` attributes is a separate cleanup if you want it.

Changes are staged in the worktree, not committed. Want me to commit, or adjust the threshold?
